A flat month isn’t your ceiling.

How Stride uses your history, and what it cannot predict

Stride uses a transparent heuristic, not a validated prediction model. It sorts your dated results and estimates equivalent times at your selected distance using time × (target distance / race distance)1.06. Equivalents from another distance are less reliable, especially without endurance training.

Only results marked comparable at the same distance are used for a trend. At least three across 60 days are required. The median of pairwise log-time changes estimates the observed trend. The most recent pair must also show improvement before a faster scenario is offered; recent flat or slower results pause that assumption. Outliers and race conditions still matter. A provisional improvement scenario uses only half the observed rate, caps improvement at 3%, and approaches a limit over time instead of extending a straight line. The uncertainty range includes no improvement and possible slower performance. Today’s run uses simple effort and check-in adjustments, not a validated readiness model. It is a scenario range, not a statistical confidence interval. The clearly labelled faster goal is a training ambition, distinct from the evidence-based scenario. It can be edited and does not imply that a plateau guarantees future improvement.

Race windows use general training-block rules (12 weeks for 10K or 16 for a half, with preparation time for recent training experience, fatigue, or limited estimated endurance). They are not a date on which an outcome is expected. Starting distances are generated from race pace and available running days, not entered current mileage. Weekly plans are templates: repeat or reduce weeks if you’re not recovering. No race history, age, or height can establish your lifetime performance ceiling.

Age is optional and used for recovery context only, not to calculate a predicted slowdown or limit. Inputs are not sent to a coaching service. “Save my history” stores your form in this browser on this device; use “Clear saved history” to remove it. This is general training and nutrition information, not an individual clinical or dietetic assessment.

Peer comparisons use Running Level’s age-specific intermediate standards (checked 28 October 2026). For ages between published five-year points, Stride linearly interpolates a reference time. This is not a personal percentile or a representative population average. Comparisons use your latest comparable actual result at the selected distance when available; otherwise they are explicitly estimated from another distance. Gender and reference selection do not change training or target calculations. Supported comparison ages: 18–90.
